published.title: The scheduled emails from my late grandfather (Fiction)
published.summary: An archivist inherits her late grandfather's computer and discovers a disturbing archive of unsent drafts detailing her daily life. But the metadata reveals a terrifying impossibility.

published.title: The packages at his door had his exact name. (Fiction)
published.summary: A night-shift worker receives strange misplaced packages at his door bearing his exact name. As the deliveries escalate, the final box reveals an unsettling truth about who has been watching him.

published.title: The Third Chair That Was Never Empty (Fiction)
published.summary: A minimalist host sets her dining table for two every evening to fight the lockdown silence. The illusion shatters when she finds undeniable proof that someone has been sharing her meals.

published.title: the app that photographed every blink (Fiction)
published.summary: A woman tracking her dry eye symptoms with an automated camera app discovers horrifying incremental movements in the darkness. As she scrolls through her nightly logs, the distance between frames shrinks.

published.title: The Quiet Room (Fiction)
published.summary: A man seeks absolute silence in an isolated sensory deprivation tank, only to discover an unexpected presence in the water with him. But the truth waiting outside the tank changes everything.

published.title: The Four Rules of an Empty Livestream (Fiction)
published.summary: A late-night broadcaster discovers that her only listener isn't just watching her live—they seem to know every move before it happens. An unsettling look into isolation and digital dread.

published.title: The Tenant Upstairs (Fiction)
published.summary: An isolated tenant keeps an audio journal documenting the heavy footsteps pacing directly above his bed every night. When he reports the noise to building management, he uncovers an impossible truth about his apartment building.

published.title: The tally marks hidden beneath the old wallpaper (Fiction)
published.summary: Stripping away old wallpaper in a historic fixer-upper reveals a chilling pattern carved directly into the plaster. A quiet home renovation turns deeply unsettling as the numbers begin to add up.

published.title: The Messages That Couldn't Exist (Fiction)
published.summary: When her twin goes missing, she keeps texting her missing sister's phone to cope. The replies bring comfort—until a terrifying discovery changes everything.

published.title: Static Feedback (Fiction)
published.summary: A sound designer cleaning up ambient kitchen recordings discovers a terrifying audio file hidden in the static. Following the warning leads to an inescapable realization about time and danger.

published.title: The Portrait That Blinked Second (Fiction)
published.summary: An artist spends weeks working on a self-portrait, growing uneasy when her reflection starts lagging behind. But a chilling realization changes everything about what she was looking at.

published.title: The Porch Light at 3:14 AM (Fiction)
published.summary: A night guard relies on a distant farmhouse light to keep his bearings during long graveyard shifts. When county records reveal the truth about the property, he is forced to question what he has been looking at.

published.title: The vintage thrift store camera held impossible photos (Fiction)
published.summary: An amateur photographer finds a vintage camera at a thrift store and discovers something impossible in the film. A short eerie psychological mystery about rules you shouldn't break.

published.title: She transcribed psychiatric tapes until she heard her own vo (Fiction)
published.summary: A meticulous archivist transcribes old cassette tapes of psychiatric sessions, growing overly protective of a patient who claims she is being replaced by her therapist. The unsettling truth unfolds when the archivist presses play.

published.title: The study app that wrote in my forgotten handwriting (Fiction)
published.summary: A college student uses a vocabulary matching app, only to find the daily lists form a confession to a break-in written in a forgotten hand.

topic_pool.title: The Infinite Staircase
topic_pool.premise: A fitness tracker user notices her daily step count hits 10,000 before she even wakes up. She watches her hallway security footage to catch a sleepwalking intruder, only to see herself endlessly descending basement stairs she doesn't own, with someone whispering her exact waking thoughts from behind.

topic_pool.title: Subtle Scent
topic_pool.premise: A minimalist living alone starts buying expensive, unknown colognes because they always arrive pre-sprayed on his favorite armchair. The twist is revealed when his security camera catches no intruder, but rather his own clothes slowly shedding a perfume he hasn't bought since the day his twin brother disappeared.

topic_pool.title: Delayed Echo
topic_pool.premise: An audio engineer cleaning up a nature podcast recording notices faint breathing on a solo track that should be completely silent. He isolates the audio file, only to realize the rhythmic breaths match his own pacing in the room—recorded three seconds before he actually inhales.

topic_pool.title: The Green Light
topic_pool.premise: A night-shift lighthouse keeper grows comforted by a matching green lantern blinking from an abandoned cottage across the rocky cove. When the coast guard visits to inspect the boarded-up ruin, they inform him the cottage hasn't had electricity since the 1970s—and his own lighthouse lamp has been unlit for months.

topic_pool.title: Dust and Shadows
topic_pool.premise: A meticulous neat freak becomes obsessed with a single fingerprint smudged on her pristine, newly wiped kitchen counter. She spends hours analyzing who could have touched it, until she licks her thumb to clean it and realizes the print matches her own whorls, perfectly preserved in a layer of dust she laid down before she was born.

topic_pool.title: Reading Between the Lines
topic_pool.premise: An aspiring novelist finds comfort in a vintage typewriter left in her rental cabin, typing out her memoir sentence by sentence. Her dread grows when the ribbon starts automatically punching keys while she sleeps, finishing the sentences with the exact words her missing roommate used in her final police statement.

topic_pool.title: The Empty Plate
topic_pool.premise: A strict minimalist meal-prepper notices a half-eaten sandwich left on her counter every morning, neatly wrapped in wax paper she never bought. She sets up a hidden camera expecting a rodent, only to watch footage of herself sleep-eating while holding a conversation with a person sitting directly across from her in an empty kitchen.

topic_pool.title: Clockwork Silence
topic_pool.premise: A ticking grandfather clock in a quiet apartment begins skipping beats, plunging the room into deafening, unnatural silences. The protagonist finally smashes the glass face to fix the pendulum, only to find the gears are made of human teeth that are currently chewing through the winding mechanism.

topic_pool.title: The Stranger's Key
topic_pool.premise: A cautious apartment dweller finds an unfamiliar brass key resting on her welcome mat every single Tuesday morning. She spends weeks trying every lock in the building to find its match, until she opens her own front door from the inside and hears the key sliding into the exterior keyhole.

topic_pool.title: Framed Memories
topic_pool.premise: A woman curating her digital photo frame grows disturbed when unfamiliar strangers keep appearing in the background of her childhood vacation slides. She zooms in on an old beach photo to inspect a smiling man standing behind her parents, realizing the man's face is her own reflection aging backward.

topic_pool.title: The Open Tab
topic_pool.premise: A remote worker keeps finding a mysterious browser tab open on her laptop every morning, streaming live audio of heavy traffic and a distant siren. She traces the IP address to her own router, realizing the audio is broadcasting from the microphone of the phone currently pressed against her ear.

topic_pool.title: Numbered Days
topic_pool.premise: An organized archivist organizes her life by writing dates on small sticky notes and placing them on relevant objects around her studio. Panic sets in when she finds a sticky note dated for tomorrow afternoon stuck to her own forehead while looking in the bathroom mirror.

topic_pool.title: Static Horizon
topic_pool.premise: A landscape painter notices the horizon line in her daily sketches slowly tilting downward by a fraction of a millimeter each day. She rushes to the window to check the actual coastline, only to discover the ocean has completely vanished, replaced by an endless grey wall painted with her own childhood sketches.

topic_pool.title: The Neighbor's Window
topic_pool.premise: A lonely night-owl passes the time by watching an identical apartment block across the alley, taking comfort in the silhouette of a reader sitting by a lamp. She waves to the figure every night, until she turns off her own desk lamp and watches the silhouette across the alley wave back with the hand she just lowered.
